paper_title: Shortest Beer Path Queries in Outerplanar Graphs
classifications: Theory of computation → Data structures design and analysis
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 2
statement: We also show that the result in Theorem 1 is optimal for beer distance queries, even if G is a beer tree (i.e., a beer graph whose underlying graph is a tree). We do not know if the query time is optimal for (non-beer) distance queries.
context: As we mentioned before, beer distance queries have not been considered for any class of graphs. In fact, the only result on (non-beer) distance queries in outerplanar graphs that we are aware of is by Djidjev et al. [5]. They show that an outerplanar graph with n vertices can be preprocessed in O(n log n) time into a data structure of size O(n log n), such that any distance query can be answered in O(log n) time. Our result in Theorem 1 significantly improves their result. We also show that the result in Theorem 1 is optimal for beer distance queries, even if G is a beer tree (i.e., a beer graph whose underlying graph is a tree). We do not know if the query time is optimal for (non-beer) distance queries. Our second result is on reporting the shortest beer path between two query vertices. ▶ Theorem 2. Let G be an outerplanar beer graph with n vertices. We can preprocess G in O(n) time into a data structure of size O(n), such that for any two vertices u and v, the shortest beer path from u to v can be reported in O(L) time, where L is the number of vertices on this beer path.
